title: JAT-78-01 — Charlie Gourd v. Cherokee Nation — Decree

“EY
FINDING OF FACT, CONCLUSIONS OF LAW AND DECREE

NOW on this 24th day of August, 1978, the above cause comes on for hearing
pursuant to the Rules of this Tribunal. The plaintiff appeared in person and
by his attomey, George Underwood, and the defendant appears by its General
ounsel, Andrew Wilcoxen. This Tribunal, all members present, having examined
he pleadings filed herein and having heard the evidence of the respective
parties doth find as follows:

Finding of Fact

(1) That Charles A. Gourd was employed by the Cherokee Nation
on June 1, 1976;

(2) That during his employment his job performance was always
Tated as satisfactory;

PS
(3) That Mr. Gourd was terminated on or about January 27th, 1978;

(4) That the reason for the termination was the elimination of
the job position as a part of a total re-organization of the
administrative function of the Cherokee Nation;

(5) That Mr. Gourd did receive all pay and allowances due him,
including four (4) weeks severance pay, within a reasonable time
following his termination;

(6) That Mr. Gourd's termination was in effect without prejudice
since he is subject to re-hire upon application and qualification
for any future opening within the Cherokee Nation;

Conclusions of Law

(1) That the termination of Charles Gourd, as a result of job
function elimination as a part of an overall re-organization plan

is “for cause" as that term is used in Article XII of the Constitution
of the Cherokee Nation.

(2) We find no evidence that the termination of Mr. Gourd was arbitrary,
capricious, or motivated by anything other than a valid business judgment
that the job function should be eliminated.

IT IS THEREFORE ORDERED, ADJUDGED AND DECREED that "for cause” as used in
ticle XII of the Constitution of the Cherokee Nation includes the legitimate
flimination of a job function when said elimination is based upon sound business
udgment.

APPEAL DISMISSED.

CONCUR CHIEF/JUSTICE RALPH F. KEEN

CONCUR
